label: prop:schur-weyl-eightfold
title: Eightfold-way multiplets via quantum Schur--Weyl duality
html:
The eightfold-way multiplets --- decuplet (\mathbf{10}), octet (\mathbf{8}), and singlet (\mathbf{1}) --- are the quantum Schur--Weyl partners of the Hecke algebra H_3(q) acting on V^{\otimes 3}.

Quantum Schur--Weyl duality (Jimbo [jimbo1986]) states that \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N) and H_n(q) are mutual centralizers on V^{\otimes n}:

  V^{\otimes n}
  \cong \bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda \vdash n \\ \ell(\lambda) \leq N}}
    V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} \otimes S^\lambda_{H_n(q)},

where \lambda ranges over partitions of n with at most N rows, V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} is the irreducible \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N)-module labelled by \lambda, and S^\lambda_{H_n(q)} is the irreducible Hecke module (Specht module) labelled by the same partition.

At n = 3 (three-strand braiding) and N = 3 (three-dimensional fundamental representation), the decomposition reads:

  V^{\otimes 3}
  \cong
  \underbrace{V_{(3)}}_{\dim = 10}
    \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{V_{(2,1)}}_{\dim = 8}
    \otimes S^{(2,1)}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{V_{(1,1,1)}}_{\dim = 1}
    \otimes S^{(1,1,1)}.

The dimensions and multiplicities are:

\lambda \vdash 3 \dim V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{gl}_3} \dim S^\lambda_{H_3} Name
(3) 10 (decuplet) 1 symmetric
(2,1) 8 (octet) 2 mixed
(1^3) 1 (singlet) 1 antisymmetric

The total is 10 \cdot 1 + 8 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 = 27 = 3^3, as required. The Hecke block dimensions (1, 2, 1) are the multiplicities of the flavour irreps, not the irreps themselves.

The N = 3 question. The single-fibre tower of the braiding and Bring's-surface chapters has \dim V = 2 (the standard single-fibre construction yields a quantum form of \mathrm{SU}(2); the Descartes condition \chi(\mathcal{A}) = -6 is compatible with but does not uniquely force N = 2 --- see the \chi-rank audit). The decomposition at N = 2 is:

  V^{\otimes 3}
  \cong V_{(3)} \otimes S^{(3)}
  \;\oplus\;
  V_{(2,1)} \otimes S^{(2,1)},
  \qquad
  4 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 2 = 8 = 2^3.

The antisymmetric partition (1^3) is absent (three rows exceed N = 2). No choice of q restores it: the row cap is \ell(\lambda) \leq \dim V, which the single-fibre construction fixes at 2, and the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantisation does not change dimensions.

The obstruction, and what is machine-checked about it. The following are verified sorry-free in QOU/Eightfold/RowCapObstruction.lean:

  • weyl_dim_alt_eq_zero_iff --- the alternating channel \dim V_{(1^3)} = \binom{N}{3} vanishes if and only if N < 3. This is the obstruction in one line.
  • decuplet_forces_three --- if the symmetric channel has dimension 10 then N = 3. The implication runs from the decuplet dimension to the flavour dimension, in that direction.
  • singlet_forces_three --- a one-dimensional alternating channel likewise pins N = 3.
  • schur_weyl_cube_split_two_three --- the channel arithmetic closes at both values (8 = 4 + 4 + 0 at N = 2; 27 = 10 + 16 + 1 at N = 3), so the N = 2 deficit sits precisely in the vanishing alternating channel and not in some unaccounted-for piece.

What that Lean does not establish. The same caveat applies here as to WeylInvarianceQDeformation.lean above, and it is load-bearing in this one place because N = 3 is the chapter's central open problem. What is machine-checked is the arithmetic of the row cap on the channel dimensions: the file defines \dim V_{(1^3)}^{\mathfrak{gl}_N} to be \binom{N}{3} and then reasons about \binom{N}{3}, with every proof a Nat.choose identity, a decide, or an omega. That the hook-content formula gives \dim V_{(1^3)} = \binom{N}{3}, and that the Schur--Weyl row cap is \ell(\lambda) \leq N, are standard and cited --- carried by the definition names and docstrings, not proved. The file's own docstring concedes the boundary, noting that Worpitzky's identity is not formalised here. So the tier is standard mathematics, with a sorry-free machine-checked arithmetic instance --- not proved in the sense the other Lean-backed rows of this chapter use.

The conclusion is nonetheless correct, because the two cited inputs are textbook. The eightfold-way classification is not "approximately available" at N = 2 --- it is structurally unavailable. This is a scope-(b) exclusion, and the invariant justifying it is the Schur--Weyl row cap.

decuplet_forces_three and singlet_forces_three run from an observed channel dimension to N = 3; what the framework requires is N = 3 supplied by a construction. That is the affirmative half, and it remains open.

Therefore, realising the full eightfold way requires N = 3. Within QOU, this N = 3 cannot arise from a single fibre. The remaining construction directions are:

  1. Multi-fibre groupoid: inequivalent fibre objects whose interaction space is three-dimensional (T3b).
  2. Octonionic G_2 stabilizer: the Günaydin--Gürsey \mathbf{7} = \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathbf{3} \oplus \bar{\mathbf{3}} provides a non-self-dual triple from \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 (Proposition).

Status of the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate. The gate is the requirement that \mathrm{Sym}^2(W) contain no singlet. Its representation-theoretic content is machine-checked in QOU/Eightfold/Sym2GateFSTrichotomy.lean: at dimension three, passing the gate forces a complex-type summand (gate_forces_complex_of_dim_three), so the icosahedral triple T_1 --- a rotation representation of A_5 \subset \mathrm{SO}(3), hence real --- fails (real_triple_fails_gate), while the octonionic \mathbf{3} is not excluded, on the decomposition \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathbb{R} \oplus \mathbb{C}^3 taken from the literature [gunaydin-gursey1973]. That the Günaydin--Gürsey triple is complex type is the cited input, not a formalised one, so the octonionic route is not excluded rather than machine-checked to pass. Whether the route yields flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} (not just colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}}) remains open.
